With Option 1, the plot plan depicted herein can be built and commissioned to support the initial anticipated 2mtpa throughput. Then, in future years when additional carbon capture plants come online in the region and their additional captured CO is sent to the T-RICH hub, identical storage tanks and 2 liquefaction equipment can be procured and installed to handle the additional CO without disturbing the 2 Page40 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version initial operation. In this arrangement, each 1mpta liquefaction train has its own dedicated set of cooling fans. With Option 2, the liquefaction train arrangement must first be optimized so that two 1mtpa liquefaction trains must share one set of cooling fans, reducing overall plant redundancy. If the plant were built with an initial throughput of 2 mtpa but using this arrangement for the maximum potential plant expansion capacity, failure of one or more cooling fans could have a greater negative impact on the plant’s operational throughput. However, this reduced redundancy does not appear to be a showstopper. It must be noted that neither expansion option provides for the same storage tank capacity buffer as the base case, due to land area limitations. In both Option 1 and Option 2, the number of storage tanks can be increased in number from 11 to 20, resulting in a total storage capacity increase from 30,000 m3 to 54,500 m3. That equates to an 80% increase in on site storage capacity, but the aggregate storage capacity of the number of ships that must visit the terminal to load CO to achieve the desired increased 2 throughput will increase by 200% with Option 1 and by 300% with Option 2. So the ability for the hub operations to accommodate unplanned delays in the vessel schedules will be hindered substantially.
